title: Feature preview: ⚡ Streamlit Fragments - Share your feedback and cool apps!
body:
Hi everyone :<nick>:!

The Streamlit team is excited to share a preview for streamlit fragments, a new feature that provides a whole new level of flexibility and control for your apps.

```python
# A simple example
with st.spinner("Doing a slow thing"):
    time.sleep(2)

@st.experimental_fragment # Just add the decorator
def simple_chart():
    st.write("When you move the slider, only the chart updates")
    val = st.slider("Number of bars", 1, 20, 4)
    st.bar_chart(np.random.default_rng().random(val))

simple_chart()
```

This is a new decorator that turns any function into a Streamlit container that can run independently of the wider page.

![partial_2charts](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/116604821/244c382e-5371-43e6-89e4-a3a3b7cdcbd1)

It will also include a `run_every=` kwarg that allows you to automatically rerun the function and update the app every N seconds.

![partial_streaming](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/116604821/17fa51c0-8b18-491a-99fd-7d8cdb0e1733)

Fragments will offer lots of new opportunities to customize apps and improve performance. We plan to fully release the feature in the next 2-3 months. :<nick>:

Excited to try? You can :<nick>: **[check out the feature preview for :<nick>:Fragments here](https://st-experimental-fragment.streamlit.app/)!** :<nick>:

Be sure to:

- **Let us know** if you see any bugs, weird behavior, or areas of improvement.
- **Share what you build:** Leave a comment with either a public app link, of your app or a screen shot/gif of the fragment feature in action. _We may want to elevate your work to the entire Streamlit community when the feature officially goes live!_ :<nick>:
- **Ideas about the best API name!?** We’d love to hear your input and ideas. If you come up with the name that’s chosen, not only will you have bragging rights forever but we’ll also send you some cool swag. :<nick>:

Happy Streamlit-ing! :<nick>:

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
@reporter This looks awesome! Definitely going to have some headaches logicking how "global" mutables are affected by these functions -- I imagine it might be similar to how an `on_click` event works. I would encourage the team to consider making some helpful diagrams for the documentation to go with this.

Will the decorated functions be callable from other UI elements? For example, if I want to have a button outside my container still trigger a re-run of the function like so
```
# A simple example
with st.spinner("Doing a slow thing"):
    time.sleep(2)

@st.partial # Just add the decorator
def simple_chart():
    st.write("When you move the slider, only the chart updates")
    val = st.slider("Number of bars", 1, 20, 4)
    st.bar_chart(np.random.default_rng().random(val))

simple_chart()
st.button("Click to update the chart", on_click=simple_chart.rerun)
```
Where `.rerun` would return some special object recognized by `st.button` such that it would _not_ trigger an entire page reload on_click but rather just re-run that partial with `args, kwargs` from the button?


I'll throw my naming ideas in the ring too, in rough order of preference:
* st.fragment
* st.watch (as in, the things inside this function are "watched")
* st.rerun_container
* st.ream | st.reamify
* st.applet
* st.section (although I have reserved this in my own project/extension as a way to wrap code in a `try/catch` block that displays an exception and then keeps running the rest of the page)
* st.factor
* st.bite
* st.independent
* st.task | st.tasklet 
* st.live
* st.cube (because it has the page's two dimensions but then also can move independently in time of the rest of the page along the "third" dimension)
* st.fu (because it's a function and it's also funny -- this one isn't serious)

-----
FYI I did also trigger an exception on the demo app at _around_ 04:41:00 UTC Tuesday, February 6, 2024; wasn't able to troubleshoot with the exception being hidden, but it happened on a page switch from `streaming_chart` to `Job status`; in case you're logging what goes on.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Thanks @participant8 !! Good idea about the diagrams. Working on early versions of some of those docs now. And thanks for the name suggestions, several of those are top contenders right now.

On your question about the button on_click - we're trying to keep it as simple as possible for the first version and trying to avoid too many callback-like patterns, although we know a fair number of advanced users like you who would be very interested in those and will definitely consider adding them later. The `on_click=my_func.rerun` is a cool spin on that pattern, I will think more about that but it's not going to be in the initial launch.

With the current prototype (and what we are likely to release) you could accomplish something similar with:

```python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import time

chart_container = st.empty()

def update_chart():
    with chart_container.container():
        st.bar_chart(np.random.default_rng().random(7))

update_chart()

with st.spinner("Doing a slow thing"):
    time.sleep(2)
    
# ... whatever whatever ...

@st.partial 
def trigger_update():
    if st.button("Click to update the chart"):
        update_chart()

trigger_update()
```

This feature is absolutely fantastic! Please bring this to the next major Streamlit release! 

`@st.partial` resolved a specific use case I had where I needed form fields to dynamically appear based off user input. I attempted this through multiple forms on the same page, then I discovered the dreaded "nested forms" issue:

https://<redacted-host>/t/cant-get-second-st-form-submit-button-to-work/36941

Well with `@st.partial` I was able to have a **single** dynamic form which resolves everything!

comments.body:
Hi folks,

We have an updated preview which is nearly-final.

* The name is updated to `@st.experimental_fragment`
* Most of the bugs from the earlier version should be fixed
* It works much better in the case of concurrent fragments or fragment interaction during a main run

https://st-experimental-fragment.streamlit.app/

We'd be really happy for anyone to try it out and see if you can flush out any other bugs or weird behavior that we've missed so far as we put on the final polish.

**[Download the whl file here](https://github.com/streamlit/release-demos/raw/master/previews/experimental-fragment/streamlit-1.32.2-py2.py3-none-any.whl)**

```
    @st.experimental_fragment
    def download_button(self, object_to_download, download_filename, link_text, after_link_text):

        """
        Generates a link to download the given object_to_download.

        Params:
        ------
        object_to_download:  The object to be downloaded.
        download_filename (str): filename and extension of file. e.g. mydata.csv,
        link_text (str): the text of the hyperlink
        after_link_text (str): the plain text after the hyperlink

        Returns:
        -------
        (str): the anchor tag to download object_to_download
        """

        if isinstance(object_to_download, pd.DataFrame):
            object_to_download = object_to_download.to_csv(index=False).encode('utf-8')

        # Try JSON encode for everything else
        else:
            object_to_download = json.dumps(object_to_download)
        
        button = st.download_button(label=link_text, data=object_to_download, file_name=download_filename, mime='text/csv', help=after_link_text)
```
